notes = 2 modified [[KLT-40S]] nuclear reactors (icebreaker type) producing 35x2 MW electric or 150x2 MW thermal }} }} '''''Akademik Lomonosov''''' ({{langx|ru|Академик Ломоносов}}) is a non-self-propelled [[power barge]] that operates as the first [[Russian floating nuclear power station]]. The ship was named after [[Russian Academy of Sciences|academician]] [[Mikhail Lomonosov]]. It is docked in the [[Pevek]] harbour, providing heat to the town and supplying electricity to the regional Chaun-Bilibino power system. It is the world’s northernmost nuclear power plant.{{Cite web |url=https://www.rosatom.ru/journalist/news/plavuchaya-atomnaya-teploelektrostantsiya-vydala-pervuyu-elektroenergiyu-v-set-chukotki/ |title=Плавучая атомная теплоэлектростанция выдала первую электроэнергию в сеть Чукотки |access-date=29 December 2019 |archive-date=29 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191229174736/http://www.rosatom.ru/journalist/news/plavuchaya-atomnaya-teploelektrostantsiya-vydala-pervuyu-elektroenergiyu-v-set-chukotki/ |url-status=dead }} ==History== Construction started at the [[Sevmash]] Submarine-Building Plant in [[Severodvinsk]]. The keel of ''Akademik Lomonosov'' was laid on 15 April 2007 and completion was initially planned in May 2010. The celebrations were attended by the first deputy [[prime minister of Russia]], [[Sergei Ivanov]], and by the head of Rosatom, [[Sergei Kiriyenko]].{{cite news |url=http://www.vremya.ru/2007/66/8/176264.html |title=Плавучие АЭС готовят к экспорту |trans-title=Floating NPPs are being prepared for export |work=Vremya Novostey |first=Mikhail |last = Kukushkin |date=2007-04-16 |language=ru |accessdate=2020-09-01}} In August 2008, the Russian government approved the transfer of work from [[Sevmash]] to the [[Baltic Shipyard]] (Baltiysky Zavod) in [[Saint Petersburg]].{{cite news |url= http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/NN-Russia_relocates_construction_of_floating_power_plant-1108084.html |title= Russia relocates construction of floating power plant |work= World Nuclear News |date=2008-08-11 |accessdate=2020-09-01}} A second keel-laying was done at the new shipyard in May 2009. ''Akademik Lomonosov'' was launched on 30 June 2010.{{cite news |url= http://www.times.spb.ru/index.php?action_id=2&story_id=31865 |title= Nuclear Power Vessel Launched |first = Galina |last = Stolyarova |date=2010-07-01 |newspaper = The St. Petersburg Times |accessdate=2010-07-20}} The first reactor, a KLT-40S design by [[OKBM Afrikantov]], was delivered in May 2009 and the second one in August 2009 by AtomEnergoProekt (NN-AEP). They were installed in October 2013.{{cite web |url=https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/akademik-lomonosov-floating-npp/ |title=Project: Akademik Lomonosov Floating Nuclear Power Plant |author= |publisher=NS Energy |access-date=2020-09-01 |quote=}} Originally, ''Akademik Lomonosov'' was supposed to supply power to the Sevmash shipyard itself and the town of Severodvinsk, located in [[Arkhangelsk Oblast]] in Northwest Russia.{{cite news |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/NN-Reactors_ready_for_first_floating_plant-0708094.html |title= Reactors ready for floating plant |date=2009-08-07 |work= World Nuclear News |accessdate=2020-09-01}} It was decided later to deploy the power barge at [[Pevek]], in the [[Chukotka Autonomous Okrug|Chukotka]] region in Russia's Far East. It was expected to be delivered in 2019, and to replace the nearby [[Bilibino Nuclear Power Plant]], which was at the end of its service life.{{cite news |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/WR-Work-starts-on-on-shore-infrastructure-for-Russian-floating-plant-0710165.html |title=Work starts on on-shore infrastructure for Russian floating plant |work=World Nuclear News |date=2016-10-07 |accessdate=2020-09-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609173718/http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/WR-Work-starts-on-on-shore-infrastructure-for-Russian-floating-plant-0710165.html |archive-date=2019-06-09 |url-status=live}} On 28 April 2018, it left St. Petersburg under tow for [[Murmansk]], where it received nuclear fuel for the first time. On 17 May 2018, it arrived at Murmansk.{{cite news |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/NN-Floating-plant-arrives-at-Murmansk-for-fueling-2105184.html |title=Floating plant arrives at Murmansk for fueling |work=[[World Nuclear News]] |date=2018-05-21 |accessdate=2020-09-01|language=en}} The ''Akademik Lomonosov'' power station was handed over to the Russian state nuclear power company on 4 July 2019.{{cite web |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2019/07/04/floating-nuclear-power-plant-will-be-key-element-on-northern-sea-route-a66285 |title=Floating Nuclear Power Plant Will Be Key Element on Northern Sea Route |work=[[The Moscow Times]] |date=2019-07-04 |accessdate=2020-09-01 |language=en}} The 5,000 km (3100 mi) towing operation through the Arctic Ocean by icebreaker [[Dikson (icebreaker)|''Dikson'']] began on 23 August 2019.{{cite web|url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5804943/russia-floating-nuclear-plant/|title=Russia's controversial floating nuclear plant sets sail for the Arctic|work=Global News |publisher=The Canadian Press |date=2019-08-23 |accessdate=2020-09-01}} On 9 September 2019, it arrived at its permanent location in the Chukotka district, the far eastern end of the Far East region.{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-nuclear-floating-idUSKBN1VZ0CY |first=Vladimir |last=Soldatkin |title=Russia's first sea-borne nuclear power plant arrives to its base |date=2019-09-14 |publisher=Reuters |access-date=2019-09-15 |language=en}} It started operation on 19 December 2019.{{cite news |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Russia-connects-floating-plant-to-grid |title=Russia connects floating plant to grid |date=2019-12-19 |work=World Nuclear News |access-date=2020-09-01}} On 22 May 2020, the plant had been fully commissioned. By that date it had delivered 47.3 GWh of [[Zero emission|zero-emissions]] electric energy, covering 20% of demand in the region.{{Cite news|title=Russia commissions floating NPP |url=https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Russia-commissions-floating-NPP |work=World Nuclear News |date=2020-05-22 |access-date=2020-09-01}} On 30 June 2020 it started to supply thermal power to Pevek.{{Cite web|lang=|url=https://www.rosatom.ru/journalist/news/teplo-ot-plavuchey-aes-vpervye-bylo-podano-v-gorodskuyu-teplovuyu-set-goroda-peveka/|title=Росатом. Тепло от плавучей АЭС впервые было подано в городскую тепловую сеть города Певека|author=|website=www.rosatom.ru|date=|publisher=|accessdate=2020-06-30}} By January 2025, the plant had delivered 1000 GWh, providing 60% of the energy for the region.{{Cite web |title=Russia's floating nuclear power plant passes one billion kWh |url=https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/russias-floating-nuclear-power-plant-passes-one-billion-kwh |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=World Nuclear News |date=16 January 2025 |language=en}} Initially, estimated costs were 6 billion rubles ($232 million). Calculations in 2015 totalled 37 billion rubles ($700 million), including infrastructure reinforcements in Pevek.{{cite web |url=https://www.powermag.com/russia-sees-floating-power-plant-costs-balloon/ |title=Floating Nuclear Power Plant Costs Balloon |first=Sonal |last=Patel |date=2015-07-01 |website=powermag.com |publisher=Access Intelligence |access-date=2020-09-01 |quote=Costs for the Akademik Lomonosov, Russia’s flagship floating nuclear power plant, have reportedly mushroomed to 37 billion rubles ($700 million), an increase of more than 300% from the original 2006 estimate of nine billion rubles ($170 million).}} ==Description== ''Akademik Lomonosov'' has a length of {{convert|144|m|ft}} and width of {{convert|30|m|ft}}. It has a displacement of 21,500 tonnes and a crew of 69 people.{{cite news |url = http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/newsarticle.aspx?id=13196&LangType=2057 |title = Two floating nuclear plants for Chukotka |work = World Nuclear News |date = 5 April 2007 |accessdate = 30 December 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110217230225/http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/newsarticle.aspx?id=13196&LangType=2057 |archive-date = 17 February 2011 |url-status = dead}} It will have a crew of about 300 people. For power generation, it has two [[KLT-40S]] reactors, derived from icebreaker propulsion reactors, which together provide thermal reactor power of 300 MW, which is transformed in two turbo-generating sets into 70 MW of electricity (gross). The reactors use [[low-enriched uranium]] (LEU) fuel, with 14.1% average enrichment, with a [[Nuclear fuel cycle|fuel cycle]] of 3 years.{{cite web |url=https://aris.iaea.org/PDF/KLT-40S.pdf |title=KLT-40S |publisher=IAEA |work=Advanced Reactor Information System |year=2013 |access-date=10 November 2021 |archive-date=13 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231013045730/https://aris.iaea.org/PDF/KLT-40S.pdf |url-status=dead }} The ''Akademik Lomonosov'' can work as [[cogeneration]] plant, as waste heat is collected. It can provide up to 60 MW thermal power via clamped pipelines for heating purposes. Peak heat delivery is up to 170 MW while reducing the electric output to 30 MW (cf. [[power loss factor|extraction steam turbine]]).{{cite web |url=https://www.revistanuclear.es/en/tecnologia-e-innovacion/the-future-of-small-capacity-power-reactors-the-example-of-a-floating-power-unit-akademik-lomonosov/ |title=The future of small-capacity power reactors (The example of a floating power unit "Akademik Lomonosov") |first=Vitaly |last=Trutnev |date=2020-06-29 |website=revistanuclear.es |publisher=Sociedad Nuclear Española |access-date=2020-09-20 |quote=In the maximum heat output mode, which is about 145 Gcal/h, the electric energy supplied to the onshore grid is about 30 MW.}} Another [[joint product]] is up to 240,000 m3/d freshwater [[desalination|made from seawater]].{{cite web |url=https://www.power-technology.com/projects/akademik-lomonosov-nuclear-co-generation-russia/ |title=Akademik Lomonosov Floating Nuclear Co-generation Plant |date= |website=power-technology.com |publisher=Verdict Media |access-date=2020-09-20 |quote=It can also be converted into a desalination plant with a capacity to produce 240,000 cubic metres of fresh water each day.}} The reactors were designed by [[OKBM Afrikantov]] and assembled by Nizhniy Novgorod Research and Development Institute Atomenergoproekt, both part of [[Atomenergoprom]]. The reactor vessels were produced by [[Izhorskiye Zavody]]. The turbo-generators were supplied by [[Kaluga Turbine Plant]]. {| class="wikitable" |- ! The design incorporates all the state-of-the-art safeguards as documented in [[International Atomic Energy Agency|IAEA]] INSAG-3 recommendation and Russian civilian reactors had not a single accident leading to a radioactive leak in 34 years.{{Cite web|title=Get the Facts|url=https://www.fnpp.info/get-the-facts|website=AKADEMIK LOMONOSOV, a floating nuclear power plant|language=en|access-date=2020-05-26}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/26/business/energy-environment/russia-floating-nuclear-power.html|title=The Nuclear Power Plant of the Future May Be Floating Near Russia|access-date=4 September 2018|language=en|work=The New York Times|date=26 August 2018 |last1=Kramer |first1=Andrew E. }} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *{{Cite web |language=en |url=https://www.power-technology.com/projects/akademik-lomonosov-nuclear-co-generation-russia/ |title=Akademik Lomonosov Floating Nuclear Co-generation Plant}} - on [[Power Technology]] official site{{in lang|en}} **{{cite web|language=ru |trans-title=Floating nuclear power plant: ready to go |accessdate=13 August 2019|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fRjYxWHbwgw |title=Плавучая АЭС к походу готова |date=13 August 2019 |publisher=[[Rosatom]] |archiveurl=| archivedate=}}] - on [[Rosatom]] Official YouTube Channel{{in lang|ru}} **{{YouTube |title= ''The Arrival of the FNHPP in Pevek'' – Official video material from Rosatom with English subtitles |id=PruXYEY1ENU}} {{stack|{{Portal|Russia|Energy|Nuclear technology}}}} {{Coord|69.7097|170.3061|format=dms|type:landmark_region:RU-CHU|display=title}} {{Nuclear power in Russia}} [[Category:Nuclear power stations in Russia]] [[Category:Service vessels of Russia]] [[Category:Floating nuclear power stations]] [[Category:2018 ships]] [[Category:Nuclear power stations using pressurized water reactors]]
